prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 1997 manifesto’s key proposals and commitments (ideological framing removed)

- Education and skills
  - Make education the top priority; increase its share of national income over a Parliament.
  - Cut class sizes to 30 or fewer for ages 5–7 by ending the assisted places scheme.
  - Guarantee nursery places for all four-year-olds; target universal provision for three-year-olds whose parents want it.
  - Raise standards via baseline assessment, annual improvement targets, “setting” by ability, literacy and numeracy drives, summer schools.
  - Tackle failing schools with “fresh start” and Education Action Zones; invest in school buildings via public–private partnerships.
  - Expand IT access: wire schools to the internet, create a National Grid for Learning; upskill teachers using lottery funds.
  - Strengthen the profession: induction year, General Teaching Council, qualifications for headteachers; remove persistently underperforming teachers.
  - Higher education: income-contingent graduate repayments; lifelong learning via Individual Learning Accounts and a University for Industry.

- Economy, tax, and public finances
  - Prioritise stability and low inflation (around 2.5%); reform monetary policy-making at the central bank.
  - Follow the “golden rule” (borrow to invest, not for current spending); keep debt at prudent levels.
  - Keep existing spending limits for two years; “save to invest” through efficiency reviews.
  - No rise in basic or top income tax rates during the Parliament; long-term aim of a 10p starting rate.
  - Cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; maintain zero rates on essentials.
  - Promote saving and investment (new ISAs; review corporate/capital gains taxes).

- Jobs, business, and work
  - Fund a welfare-to-work programme via a windfall levy on privatised utilities.
  - Move 250,000 under-25s from benefit into jobs, training, education, or an environment taskforce; employer rebates for hiring the long-term unemployed.
  - Support small firms (cut red tape, interest on late payment, improved advice/export help); establish Regional Development Agencies.
  - Toughen competition law; regulate utilities effectively; fix the Private Finance Initiative; more commercial freedom for self-financing public bodies.
  - Maintain key industrial relations laws; introduce a statutory minimum wage set on Low Pay Commission advice; union recognition where a majority vote for it.

- Health and public health
  - End the internal market; cut NHS bureaucracy and redirect savings to care; treat 100,000 extra patients with the first £100m saved.
  - Annual real-terms NHS spending increases; longer-term agreements between primary care groups and hospitals; outcome-focused quality targets; reduce mixed-sex wards.
  - Ban tobacco advertising; create an independent Food Standards Agency; strengthen public health.

- Crime and justice
  - Halve the time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders; final warning system; Youth Offender Teams; streamline youth courts.
  - Decentralise and improve prosecution services; clearer sentencing guidelines; extend powers to challenge unduly lenient sentences.
  - Tackle disorder (community safety orders), stalking, domestic violence; new offences for racial harassment/violence.
  - Appoint a national anti-drugs lead; pilot compulsory testing and treatment orders for offenders; expand prison drug recovery units.
  - Improve victim information and protections; free vote on a complete ban on handguns.

- Families, housing, and pensions
  - National childcare strategy; support for working-time limits, annual leave, and unpaid parental leave; retain and uprate universal Child Benefit.
  - Increase housing security: address gazumping costs; flexible mortgages; reinvest council house sale receipts to build/rehabilitate homes; license houses in multiple occupation; introduce commonhold; restore stronger homelessness duties.
  - Retain the basic state pension (uprated with prices); promote “stakeholder” second pensions; retain SERPS option; redress pension mis-selling; Royal Commission on long-term care; stronger carers’ support.

- Environment, transport, culture, and sport
  - Make every department a “green” department; integrated transport strategy.
  - Rail: stronger regulator, new rail authority, protect public interest; London Underground via a public–private partnership.
  - Buses via local partnerships and bus lanes; road safety focus; promote low-emission vehicles; strategic review of roads.
  - Rural measures: protect the Post Office network; reform the CAP; balanced access to the countryside; wildlife and animal welfare protections.
  - Establish NESTA to fund young talent; end sell-off of school playing fields; reform lottery distribution; seek not-for-profit lottery operator; support major sporting events bids.

- Constitutional and citizens’ rights
  - End hereditary voting rights in the second chamber; review appointments; modernise Commons procedures.
  - Party funding transparency; ban foreign donations; possible electoral reform via an independent commission and referendum.
  - Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law; strengthen disability civil rights; reform Legal Aid; fair, faster immigration/asylum decisions.
  - Devolution referendums for Scotland (parliament with defined powers) and Wales (assembly with secondary powers); elected London mayor/authority; regional chambers and possible elected regional assemblies by referendum; strengthen local government accountability and “best value.”

- Europe, defence, and international
  - Lead EU single market completion, enlargement, and CAP/CFP reform; greater EU openness; retain veto on key areas; sign the Social Chapter.
  - Single currency: decision by economic tests; any entry requires Cabinet, Parliament, and referendum approval.
  - Defence based on NATO; strategic review; retain nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral reductions; ban anti-personnel landmines; tighter arms export controls; support defence diversification.
  - UN reform; prioritise the Commonwealth; create a department for international development; reverse aid decline toward the 0.7% target; debt relief; fair trade; human rights focus; support for a permanent international criminal court; lead on climate change (target: −20% CO2 by 2010).
